transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You're carrying the valley in your eyes. Don't let the dark drink it from you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who are you, and why do you stay so close to the oil?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep your voice down. It is the only place they don't step, so I stay.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How long have you been here?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Forty years, maybe more, standing right here by the black bubbles. I stopped running and the fountain kept me alive.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You know this place better than anyone then. Tell me about the creatures in the houses.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I am not wise. I am just scared enough to keep breathing. They watch from the shadows, ranking themselves by how close they dare get to the fountain.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What draws them closer?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Fear mostly. Sound. Names spoken too loud. They perk up when something unusual happens near the oil.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who commands them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower your voice before I say this. There is a king — ancient, the kind that has no beginning anyone remembers. Everything here serves him whether it chose to or not.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What is at the gate.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: His daughter. Don't mistake her stillness for safety. She is watching for something specific in your face — if she finds it, the gate becomes a trap, not a door.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And the pale hands in the fountain.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't look at them long enough to count. They were people once. The pool hollowed them out slowly and they didn't notice until there was nothing left to notice with.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So the king, his daughter, the watchers, and the hands — that's what's between me and Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That is close enough to get you killed correctly, yes.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother Omar is being held here. I dared him to insult the well — a pale hand rose and took him before I could move.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Omar is kept, not lost. The king chose to hold him. That is different from wandering in — it means the king noticed.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my fault. I know that. Now I need to know if anything works against the dark.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light they fear. When it is called, the hands sink and the watchers go quiet — long enough to move. But it burns like a flare and every eye in the dark will turn to you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What does it do to the pale hands specifically.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Pushes them back. Doesn't end them. They remember where you stood and they wait. It buys breath, not victory.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How long does it last.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Long enough to move, not long enough to rest. Call it early and it burns out before the dark does. The timing matters more than the words.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I call it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My hands are shaking. The cold starts in my fingers when I reach for it. The square tightens like it knows.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I see it costs you. I still need the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Are you fast enough to move when the light fades? Because it will fade, and the dark will still be there.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll have to be. Just give me what I need.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My jaw aches. There was a name I used to know — it is gray mist now where a face should be. The well took it while I was thinking of something else.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Focus on the words. What must I say.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Watch that window — it just went dark. They lean in when they hear resolve. The prayer rings like a bell and everything in the dark will know where you stand.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Let it ring then. Say it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The bubbling pool is already stirring. It knows what I am about to do. One more breath.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Take it. Then speak.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give. My hands won't stop.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am listening.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. Once only. First to hold myself, second when the hands reach.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You listened well. One more rule — if something calls your brother's name and the voice is almost right, walk away. Almost is how the dark hunts.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Almost. I'll remember that. What's the one thing I must not forget going in.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the light only when the hands touch you. Not when you are afraid — when they reach. Fear is constant here. The hands are the signal.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Hands are the signal. I have it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My hands are lighter now. That is either peace or the well taking something. I can't tell anymore.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll carry your name back to the surface. Hanash, from the valley.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Just a man who never made it home. Say it where the light can hear it. Find a better end than mine.
